books.bigTheme: Beginnings and the first promise
books.placeInStory: God makes a good world, people break it through sin, and God responds with a promise to bless every family on earth through one family that starts with Abraham.
books.pointsToChrist: The promised offspring who would crush the serpent and bless all nations finds its yes in Jesus, the true child of Abraham.

books.bigTheme: Rescue and the God who dwells with His people
books.placeInStory: God hears the cries of His enslaved people, defeats Egypt, brings them out through the sea, gives them His law, and comes to live among them in the tabernacle.
books.pointsToChrist: The Passover lamb whose blood spared the firstborn points to Jesus, the Lamb of God who rescues us by His own blood.

books.bigTheme: How a sinful people can live near a holy God
books.placeInStory: With God now dwelling in the camp, this book gives the sacrifices and instructions that let an unclean people stay in His presence without being consumed.
books.pointsToChrist: Every altar and offering anticipates Jesus, the perfect sacrifice and the great high priest who makes us clean once for all.

books.bigTheme: Wandering, grumbling, and a faithful God
books.placeInStory: Israel travels from Sinai toward the promised land, but unbelief turns a short trip into forty years of wilderness while God keeps providing.
books.pointsToChrist: When Moses lifted up the bronze serpent so the dying could look and live, he gave us a picture of Jesus lifted up on the cross.

books.bigTheme: Love God with your whole heart
books.placeInStory: On the edge of the promised land, Moses preaches the law again to a new generation, calling them to remember God and choose life by loving Him.
books.pointsToChrist: Moses promised a greater prophet to come, and Jesus is that prophet who keeps the whole law in our place.

books.bigTheme: God gives the land He promised
books.placeInStory: After Moses dies, Joshua leads Israel across the Jordan into Canaan, and God hands them the inheritance He swore to Abraham long before.
books.pointsToChrist: Joshua, whose name means the Lord saves, leads his people into rest and points to Jesus who brings us into a far greater rest.

books.bigTheme: What happens when everyone does as they please
books.placeInStory: Israel falls into a downward cycle of sin, oppression, and rescue, showing that flawed human deliverers cannot fix a heart problem.
books.pointsToChrist: Each broken judge leaves us longing for a true and righteous deliverer, the King who finally arrives in Jesus.

books.bigTheme: Loyal love in a dark time
books.placeInStory: During the era of the judges, a foreign widow finds refuge under the wings of Israel's God and is brought into His people through a kind redeemer.
books.pointsToChrist: Boaz the kinsman redeemer foreshadows Jesus, and Ruth becomes the great grandmother of King David, in whose line the Messiah comes.

books.bigTheme: Israel asks for a king
books.placeInStory: The people demand a king like the nations, reject God as their ruler, and learn the difference between a king after their own image and one after God's heart.
books.pointsToChrist: David, the shepherd anointed while still overlooked, prepares us for the greater Son of David who rules with God's own heart.

books.bigTheme: The promise of an everlasting throne
books.placeInStory: David becomes king and God promises him a house and a kingdom that will never end, even as David's own sin shows the cost of failure.
books.pointsToChrist: God's covenant with David, that his throne would stand forever, is kept in Jesus, the eternal King.

books.bigTheme: Glory, then division and decline
books.placeInStory: Solomon builds the temple and the kingdom shines, but his divided heart leads to a divided nation that begins to drift from God.
books.pointsToChrist: Solomon's wisdom and temple point to Jesus, the one greater than Solomon in whom God truly dwells with us.

books.bigTheme: The road to exile
books.placeInStory: Both kingdoms refuse to turn back, and the consequences arrive as Israel falls to Assyria and Judah is carried off to Babylon.
books.pointsToChrist: The prophets and the failed kings leave a people in need of rescue, setting the stage for the King who returns them from exile in Himself.

books.bigTheme: Remembering who the people are
books.placeInStory: Written for those returning from exile, it retells David's story and roots a discouraged people in their identity and in God's promises.
books.pointsToChrist: By centering David and the temple, it keeps alive the hope of the coming King from David's line.

books.bigTheme: The temple, worship, and hope after exile
books.placeInStory: It traces the kings of Judah through the temple and worship, ending not in despair but with a decree that opens the way home.
books.pointsToChrist: The longing for true worship and a faithful king reaches its answer in Jesus, our temple and our peace.

books.bigTheme: Rebuilding the house of God
books.placeInStory: After the exile, God stirs the people to return to Jerusalem, rebuild the temple, and recommit themselves to His word.
books.pointsToChrist: The rebuilt temple is a shadow of the lasting dwelling of God with us that comes in Jesus.

books.bigTheme: Rebuilding the walls and the community
books.placeInStory: Nehemiah leads the returned people to rebuild Jerusalem's broken walls and to renew their life around God's law.
books.pointsToChrist: The work of restoring a ruined people anticipates the greater restoration Jesus accomplishes for all who trust Him.

books.bigTheme: Hidden providence saves a people
books.placeInStory: In a foreign empire where God is never named, He quietly protects His scattered people from destruction through a courageous queen.
books.pointsToChrist: The deliverance of God's people from a death sentence points to the rescue Jesus secures against a far greater enemy.

books.bigTheme: Faith in the middle of suffering
books.placeInStory: A righteous man loses everything and wrestles honestly with God, and the easy answers of his friends prove false before God answers in person.
books.pointsToChrist: Job longs for a mediator who can stand between him and God, a need met fully in Jesus our advocate.

books.bigTheme: Songs and prayers for every season
books.placeInStory: This is the prayer book of God's people, giving voice to praise, grief, repentance, and trust across the whole story of their life with Him.
books.pointsToChrist: Many psalms speak ahead to the suffering and reigning King, and Jesus prayed and fulfilled them as the true son of David.

books.bigTheme: Wisdom for daily life
books.placeInStory: Gathered mostly under Solomon, it teaches how to live well in God's world, where reverence for God is the start of real understanding.
books.pointsToChrist: Wisdom personified, present at creation, finds its fullness in Jesus, who became wisdom from God for us.

books.bigTheme: The emptiness of life without God
books.placeInStory: A wise teacher tests every pleasure and pursuit under the sun and finds it all passing, pointing past the temporary to the One who gives meaning.
books.pointsToChrist: The ache for something that does not fade is answered by Jesus, who offers life that death cannot take.

books.bigTheme: The goodness of faithful love
books.placeInStory: A poem celebrating married love affirms that desire and delight between husband and wife are gifts within God's good world.
books.pointsToChrist: The picture of devoted love opens a window onto the love between Jesus and His people, the bride He gave Himself for.

books.bigTheme: Judgment and the promise of a Savior
books.placeInStory: Isaiah warns a rebellious nation of coming judgment yet holds out astonishing hope of comfort, return, and a servant who will save.
books.pointsToChrist: The suffering servant who was wounded for our sins and the child called Mighty God are unmistakably Jesus.

books.bigTheme: Faithful warning and a new covenant
books.placeInStory: As Judah slides into exile, Jeremiah weeps and warns, yet promises a day when God will write His law on the heart.
books.pointsToChrist: The new covenant Jeremiah foretold is the one Jesus sealed in His own blood for the forgiveness of sins.

books.bigTheme: Grief over a fallen city
books.placeInStory: After Jerusalem's destruction, these poems pour out raw sorrow, yet pause to remember that God's mercies are new every morning.
books.pointsToChrist: In the depths of loss the book clings to steadfast love, the same love that meets us fully in the man of sorrows, Jesus.

books.bigTheme: God's glory, judgment, and new life
books.placeInStory: Among the exiles, Ezekiel sees visions of God's glory leaving and returning, and of dry bones brought to life by the Spirit.
books.pointsToChrist: The promise of a new heart and a good shepherd over the flock is kept in Jesus, who gives His Spirit and lays down His life.

books.bigTheme: God rules over the kingdoms of earth
books.placeInStory: Faithful exiles in Babylon trust God under pressure, and visions reveal that every empire rises and falls under His everlasting kingdom.
books.pointsToChrist: The son of man who receives an unending kingdom from the Ancient of Days is the title Jesus took for Himself.

books.bigTheme: God's love for an unfaithful people
books.placeInStory: Hosea's marriage to an unfaithful wife becomes a living picture of God's grieved yet relentless love for wandering Israel.
books.pointsToChrist: The God who keeps loving the unfaithful shows His heart in Jesus, who pursues and buys back His straying people.

books.bigTheme: The day of the Lord and the outpoured Spirit
books.placeInStory: A devastating locust plague becomes a call to return to God, with a promise that He will one day pour out His Spirit on all people.
books.pointsToChrist: The promise of the Spirit on all flesh begins to come true at Pentecost, the gift of the risen Jesus.

books.bigTheme: Justice that flows like a river
books.placeInStory: A shepherd from the south confronts a comfortable nation, exposing how religion without justice for the poor is empty before God.
books.pointsToChrist: The cry for justice and the promise to restore David's fallen tent point ahead to the just and merciful reign of Jesus.

books.bigTheme: Pride brought low
books.placeInStory: This shortest book pronounces judgment on Edom for gloating over Jerusalem's fall and affirms that the kingdom belongs to the Lord.
books.pointsToChrist: The promise that the kingdom will be the Lord's finds its fulfillment in the reign of Jesus over all nations.

books.bigTheme: God's mercy reaches the outsider
books.placeInStory: A reluctant prophet runs from God's call to preach to enemies, only to learn how wide and undeserved God's compassion really is.
books.pointsToChrist: Jonah's three days in the fish became Jesus' own sign of His death and resurrection, and His mercy reaches every nation.

books.bigTheme: Justice, mercy, and a humble walk
books.placeInStory: Micah confronts corruption and injustice yet promises a ruler from little Bethlehem who will shepherd the people in peace.
books.pointsToChrist: The promised ruler born in Bethlehem is Jesus, who is our peace and walks with the lowly.

books.bigTheme: God's justice against cruelty
books.placeInStory: The proud city of Nineveh, once spared, now faces judgment, showing that God will not let oppression stand forever.
books.pointsToChrist: The God who is a refuge for those who trust Him and a judge of evil reveals both fully at the cross of Jesus.

books.bigTheme: Living by faith in confusing times
books.placeInStory: The prophet questions why God allows evil, and learns to trust and even rejoice in God when the answers do not come quickly.
books.pointsToChrist: The truth that the righteous shall live by faith becomes a foundation of the gospel of Jesus.

books.bigTheme: The day of reckoning and the song of joy
books.placeInStory: A coming day of judgment is announced over a complacent people, ending with God rejoicing over a humble remnant He has saved.
books.pointsToChrist: The God who gathers and sings over His rescued people does so through Jesus, who saves a people for Himself.

books.bigTheme: Put first things first
books.placeInStory: Among the returned exiles who neglected God's house for their own, Haggai stirs them to rebuild the temple and trust God's presence.
books.pointsToChrist: The promise that the latter glory of the house will be greater points to Jesus, who fills the temple with the true glory of God.

books.bigTheme: Hope for the coming King
books.placeInStory: Through vivid visions, Zechariah encourages the rebuilders with promises of a humble king, a cleansed people, and God dwelling among them.
books.pointsToChrist: The king who comes lowly and riding on a donkey, and the shepherd who is pierced, are clear portraits of Jesus.

books.bigTheme: A final call before the long silence
books.placeInStory: The last Old Testament voice rebukes half hearted worship and promises a messenger who will prepare the way for the Lord's coming.
books.pointsToChrist: The promised messenger is John the Baptist, and the Lord who suddenly comes to His temple is Jesus.
